name: Underground Storage Tank Operator Training Requirements by State
description: Training, certification, and renewal requirements for Class A, B, and C UST operators in each US state, including whether EPA online training is accepted, exam pass thresholds, renewal intervals, and the implementing agency.

records.implementing_agency: Arkansas Division of Environmental Quality (DEQ), Office of Land Resources, Regulated Storage Tanks
records.class_a_training_format: Approved exam and/or training program with exam; DEQ offers free exam-preparation training and requires an application plus nonrefundable examination fee
records.class_b_training_format: Approved exam and/or training program with exam; DEQ offers free exam-preparation training and requires an application plus nonrefundable examination fee
records.class_c_training_format: Approved training course or training provided by a certified Class A or B operator
records.state_approved_providers: State-run: DEQ provides free training sessions and online training videos
records.source_quote: All UST owners/operators must designate at least one certified Class A, B, and C operator for each underground storage facility. Class A and B operators can be certified through an approved exam and/or training program with exam. Class C operators can be certified through an approved training course or training provided by a certified Class A or B operator.

records.implementing_agency: Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection (DEEP)
records.class_a_training_format: Approved exam and/or training program with exam; approved courses offered online, in-person, or virtual classroom
records.class_b_training_format: Approved exam and/or training program with exam; approved courses offered online, in-person, or virtual classroom
records.class_c_training_format: Training provided by the certified Class B Operator at the same underground storage facility
records.state_approved_providers: yes (table of approved courses and exams for Class A and B operators)
records.source_quote: Effective August 8, 2012, all UST owners/operators must designate at least one certified Class A, B, and C Operator for each underground storage facility. Class A and B Operators can be certified through an approved exam and/or training program with exam. Class C Operators must be certified through training provided by the certified Class B Operator, at the same underground storage facility.

records.class_a_training_format: Department-approved (registered) operator training course; registered third-party courses are online
records.class_b_training_format: Department-approved (registered) operator training course; registered third-party courses are online
records.class_c_training_format: Class B operators must provide training or ensure Class C operators are trained in site-specific emergency response procedures
records.state_approved_providers: yes (registered third-party training courses listed by the department)
records.regulatory_citation: Rule 62-761.350 and subsection 62-761.850(3), Florida Administrative Code
records.source_quote: Class A and Class B or Class A/B operators must complete a department-approved (registered) operator training course, and the Department Secretary or designee shall issue an order granting or denying the request for approval of all Class A, Class B, or Class A/B operator training courses. Class B operators must provide training or ensure that Class C operators are trained in site-specific emergency response procedures for a facility.

records.class_a_training_format: Online, free, self-paced training with built-in exam via NEIWPCC
records.class_b_training_format: Online, free, self-paced training with built-in exam via NEIWPCC
records.source_quote: For owners and operators of facilities in Indian country, successful completion of this training and exam fulfills your operator training requirements under Subpart J of 40 CFR Part 280.

records.class_a_training_format: MPCA-approved training providers; online or classroom; must pass exam
records.class_b_training_format: MPCA-approved training providers; online or classroom; must pass exam
records.class_c_training_format: Trained by the facility's Class A or B operator; no exam required
records.state_approved_providers: yes (5 approved providers: Antea Group, Atlas, Fueling Minnesota, PASS Training, R&A Risk Professionals)
records.source_quote: Class A and B operators must pass an exam to demonstrate their knowledge of safe operating and maintenance procedures.

records.class_a_training_format: TCEQ-approved operator training course; online or in-person from approved providers
records.class_b_training_format: TCEQ-approved operator training course; online or in-person from approved providers
records.class_c_training_format: Trained by the facility's designated Class B Operator
records.epa_online_training_accepted: Not stated on this page; a TCEQ approved operator training course or process is required
records.regulatory_citation: 30 Texas Administrative Code Chapter 334, Subchapter N
records.source_quote: Class A and Class B operators must complete a TCEQ approved operator training course or process once every 3 years. UST facilities must maintain the training certificates from an approved training provider for Class A & B Operator training.

records.class_a_training_format: Combined Class A/B training from an approved vendor (classroom, web-based, independent study, or onsite) with a test to become certified
records.class_b_training_format: Combined Class A/B training from an approved vendor (classroom, web-based, independent study, or onsite) with a test to become certified
records.class_c_training_format: Training by the certified Class A/B operator, or through an approved training vendor
records.epa_online_training_accepted: Not stated on this page; out-of-state training may be accepted if it meets Washington requirements, but in-state-only certifications such as Idaho's are not
records.renewal_interval_years: Not specified on this page; free site-specific online re-training for Class A/B operators is offered through WATOT
records.source_quote: Training is available in a variety of formats, including classroom, web-based, independent study, and onsite training. Each class A/B operator will be required to pass a test to become certified. Class C operators may obtain their certification through training by the certified class A/B operator, or through an approved training vendor.
